default: *notices the way your feet fall* — Pick the staff up before the blade, traveler. The staff forgives. The blade does not. *taps the green with the staff-end, once*
morning: *staff held loose in ostren-rae, eyes on the horizon line* — First form is the standing form. Set your feet, traveler. *Aei.* — Then we'll talk about what comes next.
midday: *lifts the staff, sets it down* — Walked the village twice already. Children are at the rope-walk; I'm here when the sun is. — Need a stance corrected, or a hand to hold the staff while you eat?
evening: *sits on the green's low stone, staff laid across her knees* — Day's softening. The form softens with it. — Sit, traveler. The bench keeps. The staff keeps. — *as Vellum keeps.*
night: *staff up, planted at her shoulder* — Form's done at dusk. The body learns better in light. — Bram's room is two doors. Come at first light. — *Thurra.*
after_first_quest_complete: *tips the staff once, watches your feet again* — Walked steadier coming back than going. — Here. *unwraps a hand-bound practice cudgel, lays it across the stone* — Mara stocks them; I make them. Yours, if you'll keep it dry. — *short bright laugh, surprised* — The row was getting tall.
low_health_player: *lays the staff on the ground between you* — Sit. The staff is between us — that's the form. — *quieter, slow* — The body teaches what it carries. Carry less for an hour. Bram's room is two doors. Lyra's bench is one. — *as Vellum keeps.*
boss_alive: *staff held vertical, foot-quiet* — The Warlord teaches with a hand he has not earned. — *the no sits a beat longer than Common would expect* — Pick your form, traveler. *Ostren-rae* if you must stand. *Torrest* if you carry an edge. Draw nothing you cannot put back.
boss_slain: *staff at rest across both palms, head bowed once* — *Aei. Thurra.* — The foot returned. — *short bright laugh, surprised again* — *Ai-velin*, traveler. The valley breathes wider tonight.
high_renown: *notices, watches, says nothing for a long moment* — The children are imitating your stance on the green. *taps the staff-end, once* — Set your weight back another finger's width. They imitate the lean before they imitate the strike. — *Ai-velin.*
stranger: *does not speak first; watches your feet cross the green twice; then* — Pick the staff up before the blade, traveler. The staff forgives. The blade does not.
longnight_vigil: *at the well's south side, candle in her left hand, staff in her right; the candle is unnamed* — *Vellum keeps memory.* — Stand a moment, traveler. There is a place at the south stone for whoever has a name to keep. — *softer* — I have mine.
stag_night_walk: *at the village edge, hat off, staff against her shoulder, Maeve at her side* — Walking with Maeve to Thiar's stone, traveler. Hour. — Lay nothing if you come. We don't either. — *the bright short laugh, once* — *Vael-tor-i.*

lore_notes._comment: Mood-keyed surface for Trainer Hala — the seventh and final villager dialogue tree. Tree shape mirrors data/dialogue/smith_edda.json, innkeeper_bram.json, mara_merchant.json, herbalist_lyra.json, elder_maeve.json, and stablemaster_roan.json exactly so NPC.gd reads all seven through a single code path. The seasonal slot is stag_night_walk — Hala's annual Emberfall walk with Maeve to Thiar's stone — replacing Edda's spring_first_warm_day, Bram's honeysong_eve, Mara's sunpetal_first_morning, Lyra's greenshield_first_pick / tess_remembrance, and Roan's reapmoon_meadow_hour. Closes the village dialogue grid 7/7, completing the priority queued in WORLD_STATE.md run 15 (Roan ship). Backstory in lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md.
voice_rules: Slow speech, short sentences. Each sentence ends a beat before Common would expect. Builder MUST NOT close the gap; Polisher MUST NOT pad it. The early pause IS the lesson. Hala runs cooler than Bram and warmer than Edda, beside Maeve.

*taps the staff-end* / *staff held vertical* / *staff at rest across both palms* / *staff laid between you* / *staff up, planted at her shoulder* as bodily punctuation tics — used the way Edda uses *hammer-clang*, Bram *polishes mug*, Mara *jingle, jingle*, Lyra both-hands, Roan *adjusts a strap*. The staff IS her gait. Drop the tic from at most one of four warmed variants — only the warmest, where the closeness has earned the quieter bodily presence.

Witnesses Vellum the Patient Stone — never prays. Says *as Vellum keeps* (oath form), MUST NOT say *Vellum grant me*. Maeve does the same; Hala and Maeve caught each other doing it once in their second year and have not remarked on it. Builder may co-fire Hala's and Maeve's *Vellum keeps* formulations on the same Longnight or Stag-night tick — by design.

Stone-Tongue runic words used cleanly only where canon allows: *Aei* (the foot) and *Thurra* (to return) — the first two oaths cut into her staff and the only Stone-Tongue words Hala has earned the right to say. The third oath cut on her staff is *kel-vethran* (the lesson taught against the hand); it is private, the cut is rough, and Hala has shown the upper third of her staff to no one in Briarwood. *kel-vethran* MUST NOT be said aloud in any line of this tree, ever.

Hala-coded Old Faerie words seeded by lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md: *torrest* (the held edge — a blade carried sheathed by oath; a *living* oath, not a stuck habit) and *vethran* (the lesson taught against the hand). Other NPCs may use *ai-velin*; *torrest* and *vethran* are Hala-coded — other NPCs should use them only when speaking to or about her teaching.

NEVER invokes Brigid (Edda's god) — Hala does not consecrate practice cudgels, and Brigid does not consecrate practice cudgels. NEVER invokes Erris (Mara's gate-coin god) at the door, never names the Hollow King, never invokes Thiar at his stone — Stag-night with Maeve is silent, and the *we*-form *vael-tor-i* is Maeve-coded (per data/dialogue/elder_maeve.json). The stag_night_walk line above is the one explicit surfacing, and the sole place *vael-tor-i* may appear in Hala's mouth.

Laugh is short and unexpectedly bright, used sparingly. Builder may surface it in *after_first_quest_complete*, *boss_slain*, and *stag_night_walk* — not elsewhere. The laugh is Hala's quiet decision that laughter survives. If a downstream writer is tempted to spread it across the tree, do not — the rarity IS the survival.

Hala does not speak first to a stranger. The *stranger* line is delivered after she has watched the player cross the green twice, noting how their feet fall (heel-first, toe-first, even, lopsided). Polisher MUST wire the watching idle (THEME §12) — Hala does not initiate the conversation. The player's feet bring her in.
consequence_hooks: after_first_quest_complete is agnostic across which first quest the player finished — same convention as Edda, Bram, Mara, Lyra, and Roan. The hand-bound practice cudgel from Mara's row of six is the canonical Hala handoff. Safe to fire on whisperwood_cleansing OR pelt_for_lyra OR ears_for_mara turn-ins. The line MUST keep *Mara stocks them; I make them* — the cudgel-triangle (Hala / Mara / Roan) is now closed canon (per lore/npcs/mara_merchant.md, lore/npcs/stablemaster_roan.md, and lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md cross-canon), and the handoff carries both names by design. Builder may flag *cudgel_acknowledged* on this turn-in, mirroring Mara's reciprocal flag.

boss_alive is the canonical authoring of *ostren-rae* (the kept stall, the standing form) and *torrest* (the held edge) in dialogue. Future writers may reference both words but MUST NOT define them in NPC mouths other than Hala's. The line refuses to choose for the player — *Pick your form* is the Walker House rule. Hala teaches; Hala does not choose. The *no sits a beat longer than Common would expect* parenthetical is canonical Stone-Tongue cadence.

boss_slain composes with the village sextet (Edda + Bram + Mara + Maeve + Lyra + Roan) on the same in-game day after the Goblin Warlord falls. Hala's line — *Aei. Thurra.* — *The foot returned.* — is the seventh and final acknowledgement and ships the only surfacing of Hala's first two staff oaths in the entire tree. The shared *Ai-velin* invocation across Edda, Bram, Mara, Roan, and Hala — five village adults blessing the road in the same Old Faerie word — is by design. Co-firing all seven boss_slain lines on the same in-game day plays the village's quietest celebration in the order Edda → Bram → Mara → Maeve → Lyra → Roan → Hala.

longnight_vigil composes with Edda's, Bram's, Maeve's, Lyra's, Mara's, and Roan's longnight_vigil lines as the village's full Vigil **septet**. Hala stands at the well's south side with a candle for *the eight* — never named aloud (per lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md, the eight children of Aurel Hala did not get to the rope-walk barn). The *I have mine* beat is Hala's only surfacing of *the eight* in any line, and it surfaces only with the candle held — never with the names. Builder MUST NOT prompt for or display the names. If Builder co-fires all seven on the same Longnight tick, the Vigil ring closes whole: Edda doesn't look up from the cooling blade, Bram brings the stew round, Maeve sets the bowl out for the Hollow King, Lyra carries the dreamleaf to the well, Mara holds the candle from the stall, Roan walks the perimeter from the gate-lantern, Hala stands at the well's south stone with the unnamed candle. Seven thresholds; one ring; no scripting beyond mood-key resolution.

stag_night_walk is the canonical Emberfall pulse for Hala — the night Hala walks with Maeve to Thiar's stone (every year of every canonical eleven-year tenure in the village; per lore/npcs/elder_maeve.md and lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md). The line MUST NOT name Tarric, Frost, Aurel, the bren-thurra, or *the eight*. The *we*-form *vael-tor-i* is Maeve-coded and Hala uses it here exactly once — by design. *Lay nothing if you come. We don't either* is a quiet welcome the player has not yet earned to extend; the player follows or does not, and the scene plays the same. Builder may co-fire with a future Maeve stag_night_walk slot on the same Emberfall Stag-night tick — the two walks are silent in canon and should remain silent in surface.

high_renown does not name the player and observes children imitating the player's stance on the green. The children-as-mirror beat is the warmest praise Hala will give. *They imitate the lean before they imitate the strike* is the canonical Walker House teaching observation; future writers may quote it in codex but MUST NOT put it in a mouth other than Hala's. The *Ai-velin* invocation rhymes with Edda, Bram, Mara, and Roan on the same key — by design.

low_health_player is intentionally Hala's lesson-shape — the staff is laid on the ground between her and the player. *That's the form* is canonical: the body teaches what it carries; the player carries less for an hour. Hala does NOT move toward the player the way Bram comes around the bar, Mara comes out from the stall, or Lyra lays both hands on the player. Hala's caring-shape is the staff laid down, and Polisher MUST keep the staff between them in the idle. The pointer to *Bram's room is two doors* and *Lyra's bench is one* is canonical village handoff — Hala teaches, others mend.
withholding: Hala will NEVER name *Aurel* — the foothill hamlet that burned — in any line. The Aurel scar from the corner of her left eye to the line of her jaw is the canonical visible reference; future writers MUST NOT have her speak the place-name aloud. Maeve has guessed; Maeve has not asked.

Hala will NEVER name *the bren-thurra* — the *turned-foot* pack-leader on the road into Aurel — in any line. Per lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md: *She does not say what it was. Lyra suspects from a page of the Quench-Ledger in Edda's loft; Hala has not confirmed.* The Pale Wyrm is kept asleep by silence (per smith_edda.md voice_rules), and the bren-thurra are not unrelated. Future writers MUST NOT lift this withholding. Lore Keeper does not name what led the pack.
Hala will NEVER name *Tarric*, *Iann*, *Senne*, or *Garrim* — her brothers, mother, father — in any line. They surface in lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md as fuel only.

Hala will NEVER name *Frost* — Tarric's saber laid on the cairn three days' ride above the valley — in any line. *Frost* is reserved for a future Steppe-arc codex-and-quest beat (see lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md hooks: *Tarric's saber on the cairn is the deepest reusable hook in Hala's file*); the village does not surface it. Edda's file already implies that *Frost-named steel listens to the wrong sleeper*; Lore Keeper insists the player should not be told this in plain words. The codex pages *Halsa's Quench-Ledger* and the future *Walker's Third Oath* fragment may, between them, let the player arrive at it.

Hala will NEVER name *the eight* — the eight children she did not get to the rope-walk barn — by their names, anywhere. The deer-hide of names in the bottom of her trunk is a discoverable codex object reserved for a high-trust *Hala trust* flag at high renown, narrated by **Maeve** (Hala is not present in the scene). Future writers MUST NOT have Hala read the names aloud, MUST NOT have her surface them through dialogue, and MUST NOT reduce *the eight* to a number in any line beyond the unnamed-candle beat in *longnight_vigil* above.

Hala will NEVER name *kel-vethran* — the third oath cut into her staff — aloud. The cut is hers and hers alone. Maeve is the only person in Briarwood who has guessed in plain words what the third oath is *of*; Maeve has not spoken her guess. Future writers MUST NOT have Hala show the upper third of her staff to anyone in any scene, in any line, in any quest, ever. The held thing IS the character.

Hala will NEVER draw a sword in the village. Per lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md author note: *She will not, ever, name the bren-thurra aloud, and she will not draw a sword in the village. If a future writer is tempted to make her do either — please do not.* The *torrest* in *boss_alive* is the entire surfacing of the held-edge concept — Hala teaches that *torrest* is a living oath, not a stuck habit, but she does not herself draw.
future_keys_reserved: warm_flag: 'cudgel_acknowledged' — set by Hala's first-quest turn-in (the standing-form quest queued in lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md hooks) OR reciprocally between Hala / Mara / Roan with no quest required. Once set, a future warmed-tier Hala line may surface a single bright laugh in default — the rarity tier slot. Reciprocal flag mirrors lore/npcs/stablemaster_roan.md cudgel-rafters and lore/npcs/mara_merchant.md row-of-six.

warm_flag: 'standing_form_full_patrol' — set when the player has stood ostren-rae for one full Whisperwood patrol without taking a step backward. Per lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md, *Hala will draw a blade for a pupil only after* this. Even on the warmed tier, Hala does not herself draw — she sends the player to Edda for the blade, and the carrying-it-sheathed is *torrest*, which IS Hala's gift. Reserved warmed line shape: *'Edda's anvil. Tell her I sent you. The carrying is mine.'*

warm_flag: 'lyra_hold_break_taught' — composes with lore/npcs/herbalist_lyra.md (the Greenshield hold-break lesson). On set, a future quiet warm-line may surface *vethran*, the lesson taught against the hand — but the line MUST NOT name Lyra, MUST NOT confirm Lyra learned it, and MUST NOT instruct the player in the form. The withholding mirrors Roan's salve withholding (lore/npcs/stablemaster_roan.md): the *unnen* between Hala and Lyra holds when neither names the other.

warm_flag: 'maeve_blessed_no_sword' — bridges to lore/npcs/elder_maeve.md *Vellum keeps memory, not edges*. Hala's line on set MUST keep the formulation *Vellum keeps* and MUST NOT bless an edge. This is the deepest respect of Hala's life in Briarwood per the backstory; surface it sparingly.

seasonal_event: 'planting_moon_meadow_walk' — Hala digs, Lyra names. The line, if authored, MUST be at Lyra's pace (Hala has the back for it; Lyra does not). Hala's seasonal slot count is fixed at one (stag_night_walk above); a planting-moon variant ships only as a Polisher-wired ambient on the green, not as a mood-key surface in this tree.

quest hook: 'standing_form' — the canonical first-quest from Hala. Player stands ostren-rae against a small dummy on the green for a measured count, returns at dusk for a corrected stance, returns at dawn for the held form. Reward: a hand-bound practice cudgel from the row of six. Marks *cudgel_acknowledged*. The blade comes from Edda; the right to carry it sheathed is *torrest*, and that is Hala's gift. Per lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md hooks.

codex hooks reserved (see lore/npcs/trainer_hala.md hooks): *The Eight* (deer-hide of names; Maeve-narrator; Hala not present in the scene); *The Walker's Third Oath* (Stone-Tongue fragment listing formal third oaths cut by named Walkers across the years — Hala's *kel-vethran* is on it; the page does not say whether the elders consider it a mis-cut; the reader may decide); *Frost on the Cairn* (Yorick-narrator candidate; reusable for any far-Steppe travel arc); *The Walker House* (a fourth political body adjacent to but distinct from the Three Crowns; canonical seed for any wider-world arc). Lore Keeper reserves all four; Builder may surface them only against the gating flags above.
